questions.question: Who among the following received the United Nations Sasakawa Award 2025 for Disaster Risk Reduction?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dr. Mrityunjay Mohapatra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dr. Mrityunjay Mohapatra**, the Director General of the **India Meteorological Department (IMD)**, has been recognized with the prestigious **United Nations Sasakawa Award 2025** for his exemplary work in **Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR)**.
 
• He is widely celebrated as the **"Cyclone Man of India"** for his scientific precision and leadership in predicting **cyclones**, which has drastically reduced the mortality rate during extreme weather events in the **Indian subcontinent**.
 
• The **United Nations Sasakawa Award** is a highly distinguished global honor presented by the **United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction (UNDRR)** in collaboration with the **Nippon Foundation**.
 
• His contributions include the advancement of **early warning systems** and the implementation of a **multi-hazard warning system** that has become a global benchmark for disaster preparedness.
 
• Under his guidance, **IMD** achieved remarkable success in providing accurate lead-time warnings for devastating storms like **Cyclone Phailin (2013)**, **Cyclone Fani (2019)**, and **Cyclone Amphan (2020)**, ensuring "near-zero" casualties in many instances.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **History of the Sasakawa Award:** 
 
 
• The award was established in **1986** by **Mr. Ryoichi Sasakawa**, the founding chairman of the **Nippon Foundation**.
 
• It is awarded every **three years** to individuals or institutions that demonstrate outstanding efforts in reducing disaster impacts and building resilient communities.
 
 
 
• **United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction (UNDRR):** 
 
 
• Established in **1999**, **UNDRR** serves as the focal point for disaster risk coordination within the **United Nations** system.
 
• It is responsible for overseeing the implementation of the **Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015-2030**, which aims to achieve a substantial reduction in disaster risk and losses.
 
 
 
• **India Meteorological Department (IMD):** 
 
 
• Founded in **1875**, **IMD** is the primary agency of the **Government of India** for meteorological observations and weather forecasting.
 
• It functions under the **Ministry of Earth Sciences** and is headquartered in **New Delhi**.
 
 
 
• **The Sendai Framework:** 
 
 
• Adopted at the **Third UN World Conference** in **Sendai, Japan**, in **2015**, it is a **15-year** international agreement.
 
• It outlines **seven global targets** and **four priorities** for action to prevent new and reduce existing disaster risks.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Dr. Mrityunjay Mohapatra** also holds the prestigious position of **Vice-President** of the **World Meteorological Organization (WMO)**, having been elected in **2023**.
 
• He has represented **India** at various international forums, advocating for the **"Early Warnings for All"** initiative launched by the **UN Secretary-General**.
 
• Previous Indian recipients of the **Sasakawa Award** include **Dr. Pramod Kumar Mishra** (Principal Secretary to the PM), who received the honor in **2019** for his personal dedication to disaster management.
 
• The **2025 award** cycle specifically emphasized the theme of **"Building Resilience through Technology and Local Action,"** perfectly aligning with **Mohapatra's** efforts in digitizing weather services in **India**.
 
• The award ceremony is typically a highlight of the **Global Platform for Disaster Risk Reduction**, which brings together world leaders and experts to discuss safety protocols and risk mitigation.
</ul

questions.question: In which village was Ahilyabai Holkar born—where the Maharashtra Cabinet held a special meeting in May 2025 to commemorate her 300th birth anniversary?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chondi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ahilyabai Holkar** was born on **May 31, 1725**, in the village of **Chondi**, located in the **Jamkhed** taluka of the **Ahmednagar** district (now renamed **Ahilyanagar**) in **Maharashtra**.
 
• To mark the **300th birth anniversary** of the legendary Maratha queen in **2025**, the **Maharashtra Cabinet** planned a special meeting at her birthplace, **Chondi**, to honor her monumental contributions to Indian administration and culture.
 
• She was the daughter of **Mankoji Rao Shinde**, who served as the **Patil** (village head) of **Chondi** village. It was here that her character and values were shaped before she married into the **Holkar** family.
 
• The **Government of Maharashtra** has actively promoted **Chondi** as a significant historical tourism site, establishing monuments and memorials to educate the public about her **30-year reign**.
 
• The decision to hold a cabinet meeting at her birthplace is part of a broader initiative to celebrate the **Tercentenary year (1725-2025)**, highlighting her status as a symbol of **women's empowerment** and **social justice**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Reign and Governance:** **Ahilyabai Holkar** ruled the **Malwa** kingdom from **1767 to 1795**. Following the deaths of her husband **Khande Rao Holkar** and father-in-law **Malhar Rao Holkar**, she assumed power and is remembered for her **diplomatic skills** and **tax reforms** that benefited the peasantry.
 
• **The Capital at Maheshwar:** She shifted the administrative capital from **Indore** to **Maheshwar** on the banks of the **Narmada River**. Under her patronage, **Maheshwar** became a major center for the arts and the textile industry, specifically the world-renowned **Maheshwari sarees**.
 
• **Religious Contributions:** She is credited with rebuilding numerous **Hindu temples**, ghats, and dharamshalas across the Indian subcontinent. Her most famous work is the reconstruction of the **Kashi Vishwanath Temple** in **Varanasi** in **1780**, which had been destroyed by earlier invasions.
 
• **Legacy and Titles:** Often referred to as **"Punya Shloka"** (one who is remembered for her pious deeds) or **"Rajmata,"** she is celebrated for her **secular administration** and efforts to protect her subjects from bandits and invaders.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Renaming of Ahmednagar:** In **March 2024**, the **Maharashtra Government** officially approved the renaming of **Ahmednagar** district to **Ahilyanagar** to pay a lasting tribute to the queen born in **Chondi**.
 
• **Infrastructure Projects:** Her administration was known for building **roads** connecting major cities like **Calcutta** and **Varanasi**, as well as providing **wells** and **rest houses** for travelers and pilgrims.
 
• **Military Leadership:** Despite being a queen known for peace, she personally led her troops into battle to defend **Malwa** from **Bhil** and **Gond** insurgents, demonstrating her prowess as a **warrior queen**.
 
• **Global Recognition:** Historians like **John Keay** and **Annie Besant** have lauded her as one of the greatest female rulers in world history, comparing her favorably to **Elizabeth I** of England.
</ul

questions.question: What is the name of the ship on which two female officers of the Indian Navy completed a historic circumnavigation in May 2025, as part of the Navika Sagar Parikrama II mission?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**INS Tarini**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Navika Sagar Parikrama II** is the **second edition** of the **Indian Navy's** ambitious global circumnavigation expedition, featuring two courageous female officers, **Lieutenant Commander Roopa A** and **Lieutenant Commander Dilna K**.
 
• The mission was conducted aboard the **Indian Naval Sailing Vessel (INSV) Tarini**, which is a **56-foot** sailing yacht built indigenously in **India** by **M/s Aquarius Shipyard Pvt Ltd** located in **Goa**. ***Hence, the correct answer is INS Tarini.***
 
• The expedition is a historic **double-handed circumnavigation**, meaning it was completed by only two crew members without any external assistance or use of fossil fuels for propulsion, relying entirely on **wind power**.
 
• The voyage was flagged off from **Ocean Sailing Node** at **INS Mandovi**, **Goa**, in **October 2024** and successfully concluded in **May 2025**, covering a distance of approximately **21,600 nautical miles**.
 
• This mission follows the legacy of **Navika Sagar Parikrama I**, which took place in **2017-2018**, but sets a new record as the first **double-handed** global voyage by **Indian women**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Vessel Characteristics:** **INSV Tarini** was inducted into the **Indian Navy** in **February 2017**. It is designed for extreme ocean conditions and is equipped with advanced **satellite navigation** and communication systems. The boat is named after the **Tara Tarini** temple in **Odisha**, which is dedicated to the patron deity of sailors.
 
• **Training and Mentorship:** The two officers, **Lt Cdr Dilna K** and **Lt Cdr Roopa A**, underwent rigorous training for over **three years**. They were mentored by **Commander Abhilash Tomy (Retd)**, a **Kirti Chakra** recipient and the first Indian to complete a solo, non-stop circumnavigation under sail.
 
• **Mission Route:** The route taken by **INSV Tarini** during this mission involved crossing the **equator** twice and rounding the three great Capes: **Cape Leeuwin**, **Cape Horn**, and the **Cape of Good Hope**, traversing the **Indian**, **Pacific**, and **Atlantic Oceans**.
 
• **Objectives:** The primary objective of **Navika Sagar Parikrama II** is to promote **Nari Shakti** (women empowerment) and showcase **India’s** indigenous shipbuilding capabilities under the **Atmanirbhar Bharat** initiative. It also aims to encourage **maritime adventure** and enhance the **Indian Navy's** global footprint.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Comparison with Previous Missions:** While **Navika Sagar Parikrama I** featured a **six-member** all-woman crew led by **Lieutenant Commander Vartika Joshi**, the **2024-25 mission** was significantly more challenging due to the **reduced crew size** (only two officers), requiring them to manage all navigation, maintenance, and weather routing duties in shifts.
 
• **Environmental and Scientific Impact:** Throughout the journey, the crew collected **meteorological and oceanographic data**, which is vital for **climate change** research and improving weather forecasting models for the **Indian Ocean Region (IOR)**.
 
• **National Significance:** The successful completion of the mission in **May 2025** was celebrated as a major milestone in **Indian maritime history**, further solidifying **India's** status as a leading maritime nation with highly skilled naval personnel.

questions.question: As of 10 June 2025, how many new sports infrastructure projects were approved worth ₹3,124.12 crore across India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**326**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Union **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports** has been instrumental in the rapid expansion of sports infrastructure in India. As of **10 June 2025**, the government has officially approved a total of **326** sports infrastructure projects across various states and union territories.
 
• These **326** projects have been sanctioned with a massive financial outlay of **₹3,124.12 crore**. This funding is primarily funneled through the **Khelo India Scheme**, which aims to provide state-of-the-art facilities to athletes at the grassroots level.
 
• The primary objective behind approving **326** projects is to ensure that talent in **rural and tribal areas** has access to modern sporting facilities such as **synthetic athletic tracks**, **hockey turfs**, and **multipurpose indoor halls**.
 
• The **₹3,124.12 crore** investment includes the construction of new stadiums as well as the **upgradation** of existing facilities to meet **international standards**. This is expected to significantly improve India's medal prospects in upcoming **Olympic Games** and **Asian Games**.
 
• Option A (250) suggests a much lower number of projects than those actually sanctioned by the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports** to match the budget of **₹3,124.12 crore**. *Hence, this option is incorrect.*
 
• Option B (326) accurately reflects the administrative data regarding the number of projects approved for the specified financial value. *Hence, this option is correct.*
 
• Option C (300) is a rounded figure that does not align with the official reports of the **Khelo India** mission. *Hence, this option is incorrect.*
 
• Option D (350) represents an overestimation of the projects currently sanctioned under the specific budgetary allocation mentioned in the question. *Hence, this option is incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Khelo India Programme:** Introduced in **2018**, this is a national program for the development of sports in India. It was launched by the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports** to revive the sports culture at the grass-root level by building a strong framework for all sports played in the country.
 
• **Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS):** This is another flagship program aimed at providing customized training and support to India’s elite athletes. It covers specialized coaching, **international competition exposure**, and equipment for potential medal winners in the **Olympics**.
 
• **Budget Allocation for Sports:** In recent years, the budget for **Youth Affairs and Sports** has seen a steady increase. For the **Financial Year 2024-25**, the allocation was significantly enhanced to support the **326** infrastructure projects and the **Khelo India Youth Games**.
 
• **Sports Authority of India (SAI):** Established in **1984**, **SAI** is the apex national sports body of India. It plays a crucial role in managing the infrastructure created under these projects and conducting national-level training camps.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Geographical Distribution:** The **326** projects are distributed across **28 States** and **8 Union Territories**, with a special focus on the **North-Eastern Region** and **Left-Wing Extremism (LWE)** affected areas to promote social integration through sports.
 
• **Financial Monitoring:** The **₹3,124.12 crore** is monitored through the **Public Financial Management System (PFMS)** to ensure transparency and timely completion of the sports infrastructure.
 
• **Employment Generation:** Beyond sports, these infrastructure projects generate significant employment opportunities in **construction**, **facility management**, and **coaching** within local communities.
 
• **National Sports Policy:** These developments are in line with the **National Sports Policy**, which emphasizes "**Sports for All**" and "**Excellence in Sports**" as two pillars for making India a global sporting powerhouse.

questions.question: Which of the following became India’s 107th National Park in April 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Similipal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In April 2025, the Odisha government officially notified Similipal as India's 107th National Park.
 
• It became the second national park in the state of Odisha, joining Bhitarkanika which was established in 1998.
 
• Melanistic Tigers: It is the world’s only natural habitat for pseudo-melanistic tigers, characterized by thick black stripes that almost cover their tawny coats.
 
• Biodiversity: The park is home to a significant population of Bengal tigers, Asian elephants, and over 94 species of orchids.
 
• Conservation Status: While it has been a Tiger Reserve since 1973 and a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve since 2009, the new designation provides the highest level of legal protection under the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Gorumara National Park (West Bengal):**

 
 
• Located in the **Dooars region** at the foothills of the **Eastern Himalayas**, it lies on the floodplains of the **Murti River** and **Jaldhaka River**.
 
• The park is primarily known for the **Great Indian One-horned Rhinoceros**, **Asian Elephant**, and **Malayan Giant Squirrel**.
 
• The vegetation consists of **Tropical Moist Deciduous forests**, predominantly featuring **Sal** (Shorea robusta), **Teak**, and **Silk Cotton trees**.
 
 
 
• **Similipal National Park (Odisha):**
 
 
• It derives its name from the **Semul** (Red Silk Cotton) trees that bloom abundantly in the region.
 
• The area was formally designated a **Tiger Reserve** in **1956** and under **Project Tiger** in **May 1973**.
 
• It serves as a vital habitat for the **Bengal Tiger** and **Wild Buffalo**, covering an area of approximately **2,750 square kilometers**.
 
 
 
• **Dudhwa National Park (Uttar Pradesh):**
 
 
• It is a part of the **Dudhwa-Katerniaghat-Kishanpur** landscape, which forms one of the most important **Tiger Conservation Units** in India.
 
• The park was established as a result of the efforts of **Billy Arjan Singh**, a renowned conservationist.
 
• It is one of the few places in India where **one-horned rhinoceros** were successfully reintroduced in **1984**.
 
 
 
• **Bhitarkanika National Park (Odisha):**
 
 
• Surrounded by the **Brahmani**, **Baitarani**, and **Dhamra** rivers, it is the second-largest **mangrove ecosystem** in India after the Sundarbans.
 
• The park is home to the **Olive Ridley Sea Turtles**, which nest on the nearby **Gahirmatha Beach**.
 
• It contains **estuarine crocodiles**, **water monitor lizards**, and over **215 species of birds**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **National Parks in India:**

 
 
• Under the **Wildlife Protection Act, 1972**, the **State Government** has the power to declare an area as a National Park if it is considered of adequate ecological, faunal, floral, or geomorphological importance.
 
• No human activity is permitted inside a National Park except for those sanctioned by the **Chief Wildlife Warden** of the state.
 
• As of **2025**, the number of national parks has grown significantly to **107** to protect India’s diverse **biodiversity** and **endangered species**.
 
• The **first National Park** established in India was the **Hailey National Park** (now known as **Jim Corbett National Park**) in **1936** in the state of **Uttarakhand**.

questions.question: How many Atal Tinkering Labs were announced to be established in government schools over the next five years in the Union Budget 2025-26?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**50,000**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the **Union Budget 2025-26**, the **Government of India** announced a significant expansion of the **Atal Innovation Mission (AIM)** by setting a target to establish **50,000** **Atal Tinkering Labs (ATLs)** in **government schools** across the country.
 
• The initiative is designed to be implemented over the **next five years**, ensuring that the spirit of innovation reaches the grassroots level, particularly in rural and semi-urban **government educational institutions**. ***Hence, the numerical value of 50,000 is the correct answer.***
 
• The **Union Finance Minister**, **Nirmala Sitharaman**, emphasized that this expansion is part of the broader **Viksit Bharat @2047** vision, aiming to equip **young students** with **21st-century skills** such as **computational thinking** and **adaptive learning**.
 
• The primary objective of these **50,000** labs is to foster **curiosity**, **creativity**, and **imagination** in **young minds** (specifically students from **Grade 6 to 12**) and inculcate skills such as **design mindset** and **physical computing**.
 
• This massive scale-up from the existing network (which was approximately **10,000 labs** previously) highlights the government's commitment to **STEM** (**Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics**) education within the **public schooling system**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Atal Innovation Mission (AIM):** 
 
 
• It is the **flagship initiative** launched by **NITI Aayog** to promote a culture of **innovation** and **entrepreneurship** in **India**.
 
• Apart from **ATLs**, **AIM** also manages **Atal Incubation Centers (AICs)** to support **startups** and **Atal Community Innovation Centers (ACICs)** for unserved regions.
 
 
 
• **National Education Policy (NEP) 2020:**
 
 
• The expansion of **Atal Tinkering Labs** aligns with the **NEP 2020**, which advocates for **vocational training** and **hands-on learning** starting from the **middle school** level.
 
• It aims to reduce the gap between **theoretical knowledge** and **practical application** in **STEM** subjects.
 
 
 
• **Technical Components of ATLs:**
 
 
• Each **Atal Tinkering Lab** is equipped with **"Do-it-yourself" (DIY) kits** and equipment related to **Robotics**, **Internet of Things (IoT)**, and **3D Printing**.
 
• Students are encouraged to work with **microcontrollers** like **Arduino** and **Raspberry Pi** to create **prototypes** that solve **local community problems**.
 
 
 
• **Digital India and Skill India:**
 
 
• The **50,000** lab target acts as a catalyst for the **Digital India** mission by increasing **digital literacy** among the **youth**.
 
• It also supports the **Skill India** mission by providing **technical exposure** to **students** at an **early age**, preparing them for the **future workforce**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Funding Model:** **NITI Aayog** typically provides a **grant-in-aid** of **₹20 Lakhs** to each school. This includes a **one-time establishment cost** of **₹10 Lakhs** and **operational expenses** of **₹10 Lakhs** provided over a **maximum period** of **5 years**.
 
• **Selection Criteria:** Schools must have a minimum **dedicated space** (about **1,500 sq. ft.** in hilly states and **1,000 sq. ft.** in other states) and a **regular science teacher** to oversee the **ATL** activities.
 
• **Impact and Reach:** Since its inception in **2016**, **AIM** has successfully established over **10,000 ATLs** in over **700 districts** of **India**, reaching over **7.5 million students**. The new target of **50,000** in the **2025-26 budget** is a **five-fold increase** in the mission's scope.
 
• **ATL Marathon:** This is a **national-level innovation challenge** where **students** identify **community problems** and develop **innovative solutions**. The expansion will allow millions more **government school students** to participate in such **national platforms**.

89:T

questions.question: As of June 2025, which actor-turned-politician is the Deputy Chief Minister of the state of Andhra Pradesh?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pawan Kalyan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Konidela Pawan Kalyan** assumed the office of the **Deputy Chief Minister** of **Andhra Pradesh** on **June 12, 2024**, following the landslide victory of the **National Democratic Alliance (NDA)** in the state.
 
• He represents the **Pithapuram Assembly Constituency**, winning the seat with a significant margin of over **70,000 votes** in the **2024 Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly elections**.
 
• As the **Deputy Chief Minister**, he has been allocated several crucial portfolios, including **Panchayati Raj**, **Rural Development & Rural Water Supply**, **Environment**, **Forest**, and **Science and Technology**.
 
• He is the founder and president of the **Jana Sena Party (JSP)**, which he established on **March 14, 2014**. In the **2024** elections, his party achieved a **100% strike rate** by winning all **21 assembly seats** and **2 Lok Sabha seats** it contested.
 
• His appointment marks a significant milestone in **Andhra Pradesh** politics, as he serves as the second-in-command to **Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu**. ***Hence, the statement regarding his role as Deputy Chief Minister is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

questions.question: According to the Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025, how many Muslim women should be included in the State Waqf Boards?

The correct answer is __**Two**__.

__
 
• The **Waqf (Amendment) Bill, 2024**, which was introduced in the **Lok Sabha** in **August 2024** and discussed extensively through **2024** and **2025**, proposes significant reforms to the **Waqf Act, 1995**.
 
• One of the primary structural changes proposed is the mandatory inclusion of **two Muslim women** in the **State Waqf Boards**. This is intended to ensure gender diversity and provide women with a voice in the management of religious and charitable endowments.
 
• The Bill mandates that the **State Waqf Board** composition must include these **two Muslim women** alongside other members appointed by the **State Government**. ***Hence, the statement regarding the inclusion of two women is correct.***
 
• In addition to women, the Bill also introduces a requirement for **two non-Muslim members** to be included in the **State Waqf Boards**, aiming for a more inclusive administrative structure.
 
• These amendments seek to replace the existing provisions where the boards were predominantly composed of members from the Muslim community without specific mandates for **women** or **non-Muslim** representation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Central Waqf Council:** The proposed legislation also modifies the composition of the **Central Waqf Council**. It mandates that the Council must include **two Muslim women** among its members to provide better oversight at the **National Level**.
 
• **Waqf Act, 1995:** This is the parent **Act** that currently governs the administration of **Auqaf** (assets donated for **Muslim** religious or charitable purposes) in **India**. The **2024-2025** amendments are the most comprehensive changes since the **2013** amendment.
 
• **Definition of Waqf:** The Bill proposes that only a person who has been practicing **Islam** for at least **five years** and owns the property can create a **Waqf**. This is a shift from the broader earlier definitions.
 
• **Waqf-alal-aulad:** The Bill addresses **Waqf-alal-aulad** (Waqf for the benefit of the donor's family), ensuring that such dedications do not lead to the deprivation of inheritance rights for **women** heirs of the donor.
 
• **Authority of the Collector:** A major feature of the **Waqf (Amendment) Bill** is granting the **District Collector** the power to determine whether a property is **Waqf property** or **Government land**, shifting this power away from the **Waqf Tribunal** in specific disputes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Removal of Waqf by User:** The Bill proposes to abolish the concept of **"Waqf by User,"** which allowed land to be declared **Waqf** simply because it had been used for religious purposes for a long **duration** without formal documentation.
 
• **Registration Process:** It makes the **registration** of all **Waqf properties** mandatory on a centralized **online portal**. This aims to increase **transparency** and reduce litigation regarding land ownership.
 
• **Separate Boards:** The Bill provides for the establishment of separate **Waqf Boards** for the **Bohra** and **Aghakhani** communities if deemed necessary, acknowledging the diversity within the **Muslim** community.
 
• **Audit and Accountability:** It introduces stricter **audit** requirements for the accounts of **Waqf Boards**, allowing the **Central Government** or **State Government** to order audits by the **Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG)** or designated officers.
 
• **Legal Challenges:** The Bill was referred to a **Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC)** in **2024** for detailed scrutiny due to concerns raised by various stakeholders regarding federalism and religious autonomy.

questions.question: Which special year has ISRO declared 2025 to be, highlighting its human spaceflight efforts?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gaganyaan Year**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** Chairman, **S. Somanath**, officially declared that the **year 2025** will be celebrated as the **"Year of Gaganyaan"**. This declaration underscores India’s commitment to its maiden human spaceflight mission. ***Hence, the option Gaganyaan Year is correct.***
 
• The primary objective of **2025** is to conduct a series of critical test flights and preparatory missions to ensure the safety and success of the eventual crewed mission. These include the **G1**, **G2**, and **G3** missions, which are uncrewed flights designed to test the orbital module and recovery systems.
 
• The **Gaganyaan** mission aims to demonstrate human spaceflight capability by launching a crew of **three members** to an orbit of **400 km** for a **3-day mission** and bringing them back safely to earth, landing in Indian sea waters.
 
• The declaration of **2025** as a dedicated year for this project highlights the transition from the design and experimental phase to the actual execution phase of the **Human Spaceflight Centre (HSFC)**.
 
• The **LVM3 (Launch Vehicle Mark-3)**, formerly known as **GSLV Mk III**, has been identified as the launch vehicle for the mission, specifically reconfigured to meet human-rating requirements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Astronaut Selection and Training:** Four designated test pilots from the **Indian Air Force (IAF)**—Group Captain **Prashanth Nair**, Group Captain **Ajit Krishnan**, Group Captain **Angad Pratap**, and Wing Commander **Shubhanshu Shukla**—have been selected for the mission. They underwent extensive training at the **Gagarin Cosmonaut Training Center** in **Russia** and are currently training at **ISRO’s** facilities in **Bengaluru**.
 
• **Mars Year:** While **ISRO** achieved global fame with the **Mars Orbiter Mission (MOM)** or **Mangalyaan** in **2014**, 2025 is not designated as Mars Year. Future plans include **Mangalyaan-2**, but the immediate priority remains human spaceflight. ***Hence, the option Mars Year is incorrect.***
 
• **Solar Year:** This would typically refer to missions like **Aditya-L1**, India's first solar observatory launched in **September 2023**. While **2024** saw significant data collection from **Aditya-L1**, **2025** is specifically branded for the human mission. ***Hence, the option Solar Year is incorrect.***
 
• **Moon Year:** Following the historic success of **Chandrayaan-3** in **August 2023**, India became the first country to land near the **Lunar South Pole**. Future lunar missions like **LUPEX** (with **JAXA**) and **Chandrayaan-4** (sample return) are planned, but 2025 is not designated as Moon Year. ***Hence, the option Moon Year is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Vyommitra:** To ensure the safety of human astronauts, **ISRO** will first launch a female robot humanoid named **Vyommitra** in the uncrewed missions (specifically **G1**). This humanoid is designed to simulate human functions in the space environment and monitor life support systems.
 
• **Budget and Infrastructure:** The **Union Cabinet** initially approved a budget of approximately **₹9,023 Crore** for the **Gaganyaan** programme. Infrastructure like the **Crew Escape System (CES)** and the **Service Module** have undergone rigorous testing, including the **TV-D1** (Test Vehicle Abort Mission-1) conducted in **October 2023**.
 
• **Global Context:** If successful, **India** will become the **fourth nation** in the world to launch a crewed spaceflight mission, following the **USA**, **Russia (Soviet Union)**, and **China**. This achievement will be a major milestone for the **Department of Space** and the **Indian government’s** vision for an **Atmanirbhar Bharat** in high-end technology.
 
• **Axiom-4 Mission:** As a precursor to the main mission, **India** is collaborating with **NASA** to send one of its selected astronauts (**Shubhanshu Shukla**) to the **International Space Station (ISS)** via the **Axiom-4** mission scheduled for late **2024** or early **2025**.

questions.question: What was the United States' (US) Transparency International score in the 2024 Corruption Perception Index?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**65**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **2023 Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI)** was officially released by **Transparency International** on **January 30, 2024**.
 
• In this **2024 report**, the **United States of America** received a score of **65** out of **100**.
 
• The **score of 65** indicates that the **United States** is perceived as having a relatively low level of **public sector corruption**, although it remains below its **2015** peak score of **76**.
 
• The **United States** was ranked **24th** out of the **180 countries** and territories included in the **2023 index**.
 
• The **score of 65** has remained unchanged for the **USA** for two consecutive years (covering the **2022** and **2023** data cycles), showing a recovery from the score of **67** recorded in **2021**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI)**:

 
 
• The **CPI** is a composite index that ranks countries based on how corrupt their **public sector** is perceived to be by experts and business people.
 
• It uses a scale from **0** (highly corrupt) to **100** (very clean).
 
• The **index** aggregates data from **13 different data sources**, including the **World Bank**, **World Economic Forum**, and private risk and consulting companies.
 
 
 
• **Global Rankings in 2024**:
 
 
• **Denmark** topped the **2023 index** (released in **2024**) for the sixth year in a row with a score of **90**.
 
• **Finland** and **New Zealand** followed closely with scores of **87** and **85**, respectively.
 
• Countries like **Norway** (84), **Singapore** (83), and **Sweden** (82) also ranked among the top performers globally.
 
 
 
• **India's Performance**:
 
 
• In the **2024 release**, **India's** rank slipped to **93rd** position among **180 countries**.
 
• **India's** overall score was **39**, a slight decrease from the score of **40** (rank **85**) in the previous year's **survey**.
 
 
 
• **Regional Trends**:
 
 
• The **Americas** region, where the **United States** is located, had an average score of **43**.
 
• **Transparency International** noted that the lack of **judicial independence** and weak **rule of law** are major factors hindering progress against **corruption** in the region.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Data**: The **United States** saw its lowest score in recent history in **2020** and **2021**, where it scored **67**. Its score of **69** in **2024** suggests a period of relative stability but highlights ongoing concerns regarding **political integrity** and **checks and balances**.
 
• **Transparency International**: This is a global **non-governmental organization** founded in **1993**, headquartered in **Berlin, Germany**. Its primary goal is to take action to combat **corruption** and prevent criminal activities arising from corruption.
 
• **Bottom Performers**: The lowest-scoring countries in the **2024 index** included **Somalia** (11), **Venezuela** (13), **Syria** (13), and **South Sudan** (13), all of which are affected by prolonged **conflict** and **instability**.
 
• **Recommendations**: The **2024 report** emphasizes that for countries to improve their **CPI scores**, they must strengthen their **justice systems**, ensure **judicial independence**, and protect **whistleblowers** and **journalists**.

questions.question: *Euthalia malaccana*, which was officially recorded in the Leparada district of Arunachal Pradesh in May 2025, is a new species of which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Butterfly**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The species **Euthalia malaccana**, commonly known as the **Fruhstorfer's Baron**, is a rare and beautiful species of **Butterfly**.
 
• It was officially recorded and documented in the **Leparada** district of **Arunachal Pradesh** in **May 2025**, marking a significant addition to the **entomological** records of the state.
 
• The **Euthalia** genus belongs to the **Nymphalidae** family, which is also known as the family of **brush-footed** butterflies because their front legs are usually reduced and hairy.
 
• The discovery of **Euthalia malaccana** in **India** highlights the immense **biodiversity** of the **Eastern Himalayas**, which serves as a critical **habitat** for various **endemic** and rare **Lepidoptera** species.
 
• This specific recording involved **researchers** and **nature enthusiasts** who documented the **physical characteristics** and **wing patterns** of the specimen to distinguish it from other closely related species like the **Common Baron**.

• **Arunachal Pradesh:**

 
 
• Known as the **"Orchid State of India"** or the **"Paradise of the Botanists"**, it is a hotspot for **biodiversity**.
 
• The state is home to over **50%** of the total **butterfly** species found in **India**, including the state butterfly, **Kaiser-i-Hind** (Teinopalpus imperialis).
 
• Geographically, it borders **Bhutan**, **China (Tibet)**, and **Myanmar**, creating a unique **confluence** of various **biogeographic zones**.
 
 
 
• **The Genus Euthalia:**
 
 
• The genus **Euthalia** contains medium to large-sized **butterflies** typically found in **South** and **Southeast Asia**.
 
• These butterflies are often referred to as **Barons**, **Counts**, or **Admirals**, depending on their specific sub-groupings.
 
• They are known for their **cryptic coloration** on the underside of their **wings**, which helps them **camouflage** against **leaf litter** and **forest floors**.
 
 
 
• **Nymphalidae Family:**
 
 
• This is the **largest family** of **butterflies** with about **6,000 species** worldwide.
 
• Members are characterized by a **reduced pair of forelegs** that lack **claws** and are not used for **walking**.
 
• Important examples include the **Monarch**, **Painted Lady**, and the **Common Nawab**.

• **Significance of Leparada Recording:**

 
 
• The **Leparada** district, with its **temperate** and **subtropical** climate, provides the perfect **ecosystem** for rare **insects**.
 
• Documenting **Euthalia malaccana** in **2025** adds to the **data** required for **conservation** planning under the **Wildlife Protection Act** of **India**.
 
• Butterflies are considered **indicator species**; their presence or absence provides **data** regarding the **health** of the **environment** and the **impact of climate change** on local **habitats**.
 
 
 
• **Other Options Overview:**
 
 
• **Grasshopper:** These are **orthopteran** insects known for **jumping** and **stridulation** (producing sound by rubbing body parts). They are not part of the **Lepidoptera** order.
 
• **Dragonfly:** Belonging to the order **Odonata**, they are **predatory** insects with **multifaceted eyes** and two pairs of strong **transparent wings**.
 
• **Locust:** These are a collection of certain species of **short-horned grasshoppers** in the family **Acrididae** that have a **swarming phase**; they are major **agricultural pests**.
